chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/leader

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's *sultan* (authority) is conditional, applying specifically to those who voluntarily follow his whispers and disobey God, rather than being absolute over all believers. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle of human free will (*ikhtiyar*), where Satan acts as a tempter rather than a coercer, allowing believers to maintain their spiritual autonomy through conscious adherence to divine command.
